spec.description: Tropical cyclones live on Kepler Plus: the strongest storm active (or any of the last two weeks) hour by hour from JTWC and NOAA advisories through GDACS, a 3D curtain of its wind and a time brush that replays it over NOAA GFS streamlines, the clouds GOES or Himawari saw that hour and the rain NASA measured from space; Mosaic charts of its intensification, and the storm among 270 of the last three seasons from IBTrACS.

spec.rawSql:
-- The strongest wind of each three hours, in the colour of its category, for the
-- hours the other filters keep (bands of wind, change, speed); in grey behind,
-- the whole life. The brush is not filtered by its own window (-time).
WITH x AS (
  SELECT time, category, wind_kt, $__crossfilter($stormFilters, -time) AS keep FROM $track
)
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 3 HOUR, time) AS time,
       max(wind_kt)::DOUBLE AS "Whole life",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Tropical depression')::DOUBLE AS "Tropical depression",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Tropical storm')::DOUBLE AS "Tropical storm",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Category 1')::DOUBLE AS "Category 1",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Category 2')::DOUBLE AS "Category 2",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Category 3')::DOUBLE AS "Category 3",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Category 4')::DOUBLE AS "Category 4",
       max(wind_kt) FILTER (WHERE keep AND category = 'Category 5')::DOUBLE AS "Category 5"
FROM x
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

-- A white tick at the present hour, under the bars.
SELECT max(now_hour) AS time, 1 AS "Now" FROM $track

spec.description: The strongest wind of every three hours of the storm, in its Saffir-Simpson colour, to two days ahead (the forecast); grey, the whole life. Brush a window and press play: the storm moves on the map, the curtain lights up the window, the GFS wind shows its last step, and the charts follow.

-- The storm hour by hour, as boxes as tall as its wind: the curtain. Every
-- filter of the tab reaches it through the stormFilters selection, on the GPU.
SELECT time, latitude, longitude, wind_kt, dwind_24h, speed_kmh, category, phase
FROM $track

-- The whole track, under the curtain, to the end of the forecast. Its time and
-- name are renamed so that no filter of the tab lands on it.
SELECT time AS fix_time, storm AS track, latitude, longitude
FROM $track
ORDER BY time

-- The storm itself, at the end of the window. Its columns are renamed so that
-- only the time window lands on it.
SELECT time, storm, latitude, longitude, wind_kt AS wind, category AS stage
FROM $track
ORDER BY time

-- The satellite under the storm, when GOES-West is the one that sees it best
-- (the storm's last position west of 106° W; one of three queries, one a satellite,
-- and only the storm's own answers): NASA GIBS's clean infrared (band 13), cloud
-- tops coloured by how cold they are, one picture an hour over the storm's life.
-- The map's clock picks the picture and the browser asks GIBS for it (WMS);
-- this query only says which moments to ask for. GIBS lists the moments it
-- holds (DescribeDomains); each hour gets the latest picture of the hour and a
-- half before it, so the present hour has one about an hour old. An hour with
-- none (a long gap, the forecast) points at itself, which GIBS answers with a
-- transparent picture: the map never passes an old picture off as a later hour.
-- Off with the Satellite switch. None of the three sees the eastern Atlantic
-- and the western Indian Ocean well, and GIBS has no Meteosat.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          since: date_trunc('hour', strptime(f ->> '$.properties.fromdate', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'))}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);
SET VARIABLE sat = (
  SELECT {layer: layer,
          since: since,
          domains: format('https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wmts/epsg4326/best/1.0.0/{}/default/2km/all/{}--{}.xml',
                          layer, strftime(since, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'),
                          strftime(date_trunc('hour', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') + INTERVAL 1 HOUR, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))}
  FROM (SELECT greatest(getvariable('storm').since, date_trunc('hour', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - INTERVAL 14 DAY) AS since,
               'GOES-West_ABI_Band13_Clean_Infrared' AS layer, getvariable('storm').lon AS lon)
  WHERE lon < -106 AND lon >= -178 AND $satellite = 'on');
WITH ranges AS (
  -- "start/end/PT10M" ranges, comma-separated; the first may start on a bare date.
  SELECT str_split(unnest(str_split(regexp_extract(content, '<Domain>([^<]*)</Domain>', 1), ',')), '/') AS r
  -- Switched off, or another satellite's storm: no file to read, no rows.
  FROM read_text(CASE WHEN getvariable('sat') IS NULL THEN []::VARCHAR[] ELSE [getvariable('sat').domains] END)
),
moments AS (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(replace(r[1], 'Z', '')::TIMESTAMP,
                                replace(coalesce(r[2], r[1]), 'Z', '')::TIMESTAMP,
                                to_minutes(coalesce(regexp_extract(r[3], 'PT([0-9]+)M', 1), '10')::INTEGER))) AS m
  FROM ranges
),
-- GIBS lists a moment some half hour before it can draw it: the last hour's
-- are left out.
ready AS (
  SELECT m FROM moments WHERE m <= (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
),
hours AS (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(getvariable('sat').since,
                                date_trunc('hour', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') + INTERVAL 48 HOUR,
                                INTERVAL 1 HOUR)) AS h
)
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(max(m), h)            AS time,
         'https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wms/epsg3857/best/wms.cgi' AS wms_url,
         'GOES-West_ABI_Band13_Clean_Infrared'                               AS wms_layer
  FROM hours LEFT JOIN ready ON m > h - INTERVAL 90 MINUTE AND m <= h
  GROUP BY h
)
UNION ALL
-- And one moment long before any storm, always: the WMS layer stays on the map,
-- hidden while it has no moment in the window, so picking a storm in another
-- basin or flipping the switch changes only its moments. A layer that came
-- and went with them would be rebuilt each time, and the map does not always
-- manage that.
SELECT TIMESTAMP '2000-01-01', 'https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wms/epsg3857/best/wms.cgi', 'GOES-West_ABI_Band13_Clean_Infrared'

-- The storm picked above, from GDACS's list of tropical cyclones: its last
-- position and the episode (the advisory) GDACS drew last. Through the gateway
-- (feeds), which keeps every GDACS answer a quarter of an hour: GDACS takes
-- 3 to 15 s to build each, and the panels here ask for the same ones nine times.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {id: f ->> '$.properties.eventid',
          episode: f ->> '$.properties.episodeid',
          lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          lat: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);
-- Its advisories are in a "timeline" whose id only the event's own data gives.
SET VARIABLE timeline = (
  SELECT regexp_extract(j ->> '$.properties.impacts[0].resource.timeline', 'id=([0-9]+)', 1)
  FROM read_json_objects('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventdata?eventtype=TC&eventid=' || getvariable('storm').id) AS t(j));
-- GDACS's geometry of the latest episode: the forecast's cone of uncertainty,
-- and the swath of the track (past and forecast) where the advisories put
-- winds over 60, 90 and 120 km/h: about 34, 50 and 64 knots, the radii JTWC
-- and NHC give. Simplified to about a kilometre, a tenth of the bytes.
WITH parts AS (
  SELECT json_extract_string(f, '$.properties.Class')       AS class,
         json_extract_string(f, '$.properties.featuretype') AS featuretype,
         json_extract(f, '$.geometry')                       AS geometry
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/polygons/getgeometry?eventtype=TC&eventid=' || getvariable('storm').id
                       || '&episodeid=' || getvariable('storm').episode,
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}, maximum_object_size = 64000000))
)
SELECT CASE class WHEN 'Poly_Cones'  THEN 'Forecast cone'
                  WHEN 'Poly_Green'  THEN 'Winds over 60 km/h'
                  WHEN 'Poly_Orange' THEN 'Winds over 90 km/h'
                  ELSE 'Winds over 120 km/h' END                          AS area,
       CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(geometry), 0.01)) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM parts
-- The swath is the three polygons with no time of their own; the radii drawn
-- per forecast time (featuretype WindRadii) are left out.
WHERE class = 'Poly_Cones'
   OR (class IN ('Poly_Green', 'Poly_Orange', 'Poly_Red') AND featuretype IS NULL)
-- Under one another: the widest first.
ORDER BY CASE class WHEN 'Poly_Cones' THEN 0 WHEN 'Poly_Green' THEN 1 WHEN 'Poly_Orange' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

-- Where GFS puts the storm, against where the advisories put it, at each of
-- GFS steps: the same ERDDAP answer as the wind (G).
-- The storm picked above, from GDACS's list of tropical cyclones: its last
-- position and the episode (the advisory) GDACS drew last. Through the gateway
-- (feeds), which keeps every GDACS answer a quarter of an hour: GDACS takes
-- 3 to 15 s to build each, and the panels here ask for the same ones nine times.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {id: f ->> '$.properties.eventid',
          episode: f ->> '$.properties.episodeid',
          name: regexp_replace(f ->> '$.properties.eventname', '-[0-9]+$', ''),
          lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          lat: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);
-- Its advisories are in a "timeline" whose id only the event's own data gives.
SET VARIABLE timeline = (
  SELECT regexp_extract(j ->> '$.properties.impacts[0].resource.timeline', 'id=([0-9]+)', 1)
  FROM read_json_objects('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventdata?eventtype=TC&eventid=' || getvariable('storm').id) AS t(j));
-- The GFS boxes, one a day of the storm's life (its last nine days at most, to
-- two days ahead): 15 degrees of latitude and 20 of longitude around where the
-- storm was, or will be, that day, on whole degrees. Past days every six hours
-- (GFS's analyses), today and the forecast every three. A past day's URL stays
-- the same, so the gateway answers it from its cache; ERDDAP takes a second or
-- two for each of the others.
SET VARIABLE gfs = (
  WITH items AS (
    SELECT strptime(i ->> 'advisory_datetime', '%d %b %Y %H:%M') AS time,
           (i ->> 'latitude')::DOUBLE AS lat,
           (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE + 360 * round((getvariable('storm').lon - (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE) / 360) AS lon
    FROM (SELECT unnest(channel.item) AS i
          FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/export/gettimeline?id=' || getvariable('timeline'),
                         columns = {'channel': 'STRUCT(item JSON[])'}))
  ),
  span AS (
    SELECT least(max(time), time_bucket(INTERVAL 3 HOUR, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - INTERVAL 90 MINUTE)
                            + INTERVAL 48 HOUR) AS t_end,
           greatest(min(time), t_end - INTERVAL 9 DAY) AS t_start,
           date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS today
    FROM items
  ),
  days AS (
    SELECT unnest(generate_series(date_trunc('day', t_start), date_trunc('day', t_end), INTERVAL 1 DAY)) AS d,
           t_start, t_end, today
    FROM span
  ),
  chunks AS (
    SELECT d, d < today AS past,
           greatest(d, time_bucket(CASE WHEN past THEN INTERVAL 6 HOUR ELSE INTERVAL 3 HOUR END, t_start)) AS a,
           least(d + INTERVAL 21 HOUR, t_end) AS b
    FROM days
  ),
  -- Where the storm is that day: its fixes from six hours before to six after.
  boxes AS (
    SELECT c.d, c.past, c.a, c.b,
           coalesce(min(i.lat), getvariable('storm').lat) AS lat0, coalesce(max(i.lat), getvariable('storm').lat) AS lat1,
           coalesce(min(i.lon), getvariable('storm').lon) AS lon0, coalesce(max(i.lon), getvariable('storm').lon) AS lon1
    FROM chunks c
    LEFT JOIN items i ON i.time BETWEEN c.d - INTERVAL 6 HOUR AND c.d + INTERVAL 30 HOUR
    GROUP BY ALL
  ),
  urls AS (
    -- ERDDAP's longitudes run from 0 to 360: `shift` takes the box there and
    -- brings its cells back beside the track. A box across 0 degrees is cut there.
    SELECT d, 360 * floor(getvariable('storm').lon / 360) AS shift,
           format('http://feeds/erddap/griddap/ncep_global.csv0?ugrd10m{0},vgrd10m{0},prmslmsl{0},pratesfc{0}',
                  format('%5B({0}):{1}:({2})%5D%5B({3}):2:({4})%5D%5B({5}):2:({6})%5D',
                         strftime(a, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'), CASE WHEN past THEN 2 ELSE 1 END, strftime(b, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'),
                         greatest(-89, floor(lat0) - 15)::INTEGER, least(89, ceil(lat1) + 15)::INTEGER,
                         greatest(0, floor(lon0 - shift) - 20)::INTEGER, least(359, ceil(lon1 - shift) + 20)::INTEGER)) AS url
    FROM boxes
  )
  SELECT {shift: any_value(shift), urls: list(url ORDER BY d)} FROM urls);
WITH
-- One row per fix: each advisory's position, then the latest advisory's
-- forecast. GDACS gives the winds in m/s; the advisories give whole knots, so
-- they round back exactly. Longitudes are unwrapped around the storm's last
-- position, so a track across the antimeridian stays one line.

  SELECT strptime(i ->> 'advisory_datetime', '%d %b %Y %H:%M')                    AS time,
         i ->> 'actual' = 'True'                                                  AS observed,
         (i ->> 'latitude')::DOUBLE                                               AS latitude,
         (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE
           + 360 * round((getvariable('storm').lon - (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE) / 360) AS longitude,
         round((i ->> 'wind_speed')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS wind_kt,
         round((i ->> 'wind_gusts')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS gust_kt,
         nullif((i ->> 'pressure')::DOUBLE, 0)                                    AS pressure_hpa,
         TRY_CAST(i ->> 'pop39' AS BIGINT)                                        AS people_39mph
  FROM (SELECT unnest(channel.item) AS i
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/export/gettimeline?id=' || getvariable('timeline'),
                       columns = {'channel': 'STRUCT(item JSON[])'}))
  -- A time given twice (an observed fix and an old forecast for it) keeps the fix.
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY time ORDER BY observed DESC) = 1
),
grid AS (
  SELECT column0 AS time, column1 AS latitude, column2 + getvariable('gfs').shift AS longitude, column5 / 100 AS pressure_hpa
  FROM read_csv(getvariable('gfs').urls,
                header = false,
                columns = {'column0': 'TIMESTAMP', 'column1': 'DOUBLE', 'column2': 'DOUBLE', 'column3': 'DOUBLE',
                           'column4': 'DOUBLE', 'column5': 'DOUBLE', 'column6': 'DOUBLE'},
                nullstr = 'NaN')
  WHERE column5 IS NOT NULL
),
steps AS (SELECT DISTINCT time FROM grid),
-- The advisory's position at each GFS step, between the two fixes around it,
-- in a straight line: six or twelve hours apart, the fixes are close enough.

  SELECT s.time,
         a.latitude + (b.latitude - a.latitude) * f.k    AS latitude,
         a.longitude + (b.longitude - a.longitude) * f.k AS longitude,
         a.wind_kt + (b.wind_kt - a.wind_kt) * f.k       AS wind_kt
  FROM steps s
  JOIN fixes a ON a.time = (SELECT max(time) FROM fixes WHERE time <= s.time)
  JOIN fixes b ON b.time = (SELECT min(time) FROM fixes WHERE time >= s.time)
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT CASE WHEN b.time = a.time THEN 0
                                  ELSE epoch(s.time - a.time) / epoch(b.time - a.time) END AS k) f
),
-- GFS's own centre: the lowest pressure within three degrees of the advisory's
-- position at the same step, so that another low in the box is never taken.

  SELECT o.time, arg_min(g.latitude, g.pressure_hpa) AS latitude, arg_min(g.longitude, g.pressure_hpa) AS longitude,
         min(g.pressure_hpa) AS pressure_hpa
  FROM official o
  JOIN grid g ON g.time = o.time AND abs(g.latitude - o.latitude) <= 3 AND abs(g.longitude - o.longitude) <= 3
  GROUP BY o.time
),

  SELECT o.time, o.latitude AS o_lat, o.longitude AS o_lon, round(o.wind_kt) AS o_wind,
         m.latitude AS m_lat, m.longitude AS m_lon, round(m.pressure_hpa, 1) AS m_pres,
         round(ST_Distance_Sphere(ST_Point(o.latitude, o.longitude), ST_Point(m.latitude, m.longitude)) / 1000) AS apart_km
  FROM official o JOIN model m USING (time)
)

-- storm, and where GFS puts its low; the tooltip says how far apart they are.

FROM paired
UNION ALL

FROM paired
ORDER BY time, centre

  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);

-- two days ahead): 15 degrees of latitude and 20 of longitude around where the
-- storm was, or will be, that day, on whole degrees. Past days every six hours

  WITH items AS (
    SELECT strptime(i ->> 'advisory_datetime', '%d %b %Y %H:%M') AS time,
           (i ->> 'latitude')::DOUBLE AS lat,

          FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/export/gettimeline?id=' || getvariable('timeline'),
                         columns = {'channel': 'STRUCT(item JSON[])'}))

  span AS (
    SELECT least(max(time), time_bucket(INTERVAL 3 HOUR, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - INTERVAL 90 MINUTE)

           format('http://feeds/erddap/griddap/ncep_global.csv0?ugrd10m{0},vgrd10m{0},prmslmsl{0},pratesfc{0}',
                  format('%5B({0}):{1}:({2})%5D%5B({3}):2:({4})%5D%5B({5}):2:({6})%5D',

    FROM boxes

       column1                                 AS latitude,
       column2 + getvariable('gfs').shift      AS longitude,
       column3                                 AS u,
       column4                                 AS v,
       round(sqrt(column3 * column3 + column4 * column4) * 1.943844) AS gfs_wind_kt,
       column5 / 100                           AS pressure_hpa   -- Pa; the isobars come from their own query (I)
FROM read_csv(getvariable('gfs').urls,

-- days, from the latest advisory: NHC's or JTWC's, in bands of ten percent, as
-- Esri's Living Atlas publishes them (Active Hurricanes, Cyclones and

-- switch.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          lat: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',

  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);

  || '?where=1%3D1&outFields=PWIND120&geometry={},{},{},{}&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326'
  || '&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&outSR=4326&maxAllowableOffset=0.02&geometryPrecision=3&f=geojson',

spec.rawSql:
-- The storm picked above, from GDACS's list of tropical cyclones: its last
-- position and the episode (the advisory) GDACS drew last. Through the gateway
-- (feeds), which keeps every GDACS answer a quarter of an hour: GDACS takes
-- 3 to 15 s to build each, and the panels here ask for the same ones nine times.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {id: f ->> '$.properties.eventid',
          episode: f ->> '$.properties.episodeid',
          lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          lat: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);
-- Its advisories are in a "timeline" whose id only the event's own data gives.
SET VARIABLE timeline = (
  SELECT regexp_extract(j ->> '$.properties.impacts[0].resource.timeline', 'id=([0-9]+)', 1)
  FROM read_json_objects('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventdata?eventtype=TC&eventid=' || getvariable('storm').id) AS t(j));
WITH
-- One row per fix: each advisory's position, then the latest advisory's
-- forecast. GDACS gives the winds in m/s; the advisories give whole knots, so
-- they round back exactly. Longitudes are unwrapped around the storm's last
-- position, so a track across the antimeridian stays one line.
fixes AS (
  SELECT strptime(i ->> 'advisory_datetime', '%d %b %Y %H:%M')                    AS time,
         i ->> 'actual' = 'True'                                                  AS observed,
         (i ->> 'latitude')::DOUBLE                                               AS latitude,
         (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE
           + 360 * round((getvariable('storm').lon - (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE) / 360) AS longitude,
         round((i ->> 'wind_speed')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS wind_kt,
         round((i ->> 'wind_gusts')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS gust_kt,
         nullif((i ->> 'pressure')::DOUBLE, 0)                                    AS pressure_hpa,
         TRY_CAST(i ->> 'pop39' AS BIGINT)                                        AS people_39mph
  FROM (SELECT unnest(channel.item) AS i
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/export/gettimeline?id=' || getvariable('timeline'),
                       columns = {'channel': 'STRUCT(item JSON[])'}))
  -- A time given twice (an observed fix and an old forecast for it) keeps the fix.
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY time ORDER BY observed DESC) = 1
),
last2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM fixes WHERE observed ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 2
),
now_ AS (SELECT * FROM last2 ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1),
before AS (SELECT * FROM last2 ORDER BY time LIMIT 1),
-- Heading and speed from the fix before to the last one, on the sphere.
motion AS (
  SELECT degrees(atan2(sin(radians(n.longitude - b.longitude)) * cos(radians(n.latitude)),
                       cos(radians(b.latitude)) * sin(radians(n.latitude))
                       - sin(radians(b.latitude)) * cos(radians(n.latitude)) * cos(radians(n.longitude - b.longitude)))) AS bearing,
         ST_Distance_Sphere(ST_Point(b.latitude, b.longitude), ST_Point(n.latitude, n.longitude)) / 1000
           / nullif(epoch(n.time - b.time) / 3600, 0) AS kmh
  FROM now_ n, before b
)
-- The last advisory of the storm picked above, as the stats in the first row show it.
SELECT n.time                                                          AS "Last advisory",
       n.wind_kt                                                       AS "Sustained wind",
       n.gust_kt                                                       AS "Gusts",
       -- Saffir-Simpson, on the advisory's 1-minute sustained wind in knots.
       CASE WHEN n.wind_kt >= 137 THEN 'Category 5' WHEN n.wind_kt >= 113 THEN 'Category 4'
            WHEN n.wind_kt >= 96 THEN 'Category 3' WHEN n.wind_kt >= 83 THEN 'Category 2'
            WHEN n.wind_kt >= 64 THEN 'Category 1' WHEN n.wind_kt >= 34 THEN 'Tropical storm'
            ELSE 'Tropical depression' END                                 AS "Category",
       CASE WHEN m.kmh IS NULL OR m.kmh < 2 THEN 'Stationary'
            ELSE ['N','NNE','NE','ENE','E','ESE','SE','SSE','S','SSW','SW','WSW','W','WNW','NW','NNW'][
                   ((round(((m.bearing + 360) % 360) / 22.5)::INTEGER % 16) + 1)]
                 || ' at ' || round(m.kmh)::INTEGER || ' km/h' END   AS "Moving",
       n.people_39mph                                                  AS "People in 39 mph winds"
FROM now_ n, motion m

-- Every storm of the last two weeks, from GDACS's list; a click on a name
-- shows it on the map.
WITH
events AS (
  SELECT f ->> '$.properties.eventid'                                  AS id,
         regexp_replace(f ->> '$.properties.eventname', '-[0-9]+$', '') AS name,
         f ->> '$.properties.alertlevel'                               AS alert,
         f ->> '$.properties.source'                                   AS source,
         nullif(f ->> '$.properties.country', '')                      AS countries,
         strptime(f ->> '$.properties.fromdate', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')  AS first_advisory,
         strptime(f ->> '$.properties.todate', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')    AS last_advisory,
         -- GDACS's severity is the strongest wind of the storm's life, in km/h.
         round((f -> '$.properties.severitydata.severity')::DOUBLE / 1.852)::INTEGER AS peak_kt,
         (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE                    AS latitude,
         (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE                    AS longitude
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
),
-- Active: an advisory in the last day. Advisories come every six hours (three
-- near a coast), so a storm a day without one has ended.
recent AS (
  SELECT *, last_advisory >= now()::TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 1 DAY AS active
  FROM events
  WHERE last_advisory >= now()::TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 14 DAY
)
SELECT name AS "Storm", id AS "id", peak_kt AS "Peak kt", alert AS "Alert",
       last_advisory AS "Last advisory", countries AS "Countries"
FROM recent
ORDER BY active DESC, CASE WHEN active THEN -peak_kt END, last_advisory DESC

options.content: **Tropical cyclones, live.** The storm picked in **Storm** (the strongest active one by default), hour by hour from the JTWC and NOAA advisories through [GDACS](https://www.gdacs.org), over **NOAA GFS** streamlines, rain and isobars over its life and the next two days, and the **clouds** seen from space. **Brush the bar below and press play**: the storm moves, its 3D curtain of wind lights up, the wind field follows. **Brush the charts** to keep a band of wind, of intensification or of speed. The second tab sets it among 270 storms of the last three seasons.

**Advisories.** [GDACS](https://www.gdacs.org) (the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System of the UN and the European Commission’s JRC) gathers the advisories of the [Joint Typhoon Warning Center](https://www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/jtwc.html) and of NOAA’s [National Hurricane Center](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov) and Central Pacific Hurricane Center, every six hours (three near a coast). From its API this reads the list of storms, each storm’s *timeline* (position, 1-minute sustained wind and gusts of every advisory, and the latest one’s forecast to five days) and the geometry of its latest advisory (cone of uncertainty and wind swath). GDACS gives winds in m/s; they are shown in knots, which the advisories use. A storm is **active** when its last advisory is less than a day old. Free to use with attribution; not an official warning: for that, go to the agency of the basin.

**Hour by hour.** Between two advisories (six hours apart) and two forecast times (twelve), position and wind are drawn in a straight line; the forward speed is the distance between the two over the time between them. The 24-hour change of wind compares each hour with the same hour the day before.

**The last three seasons** come from [IBTrACS](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/international-best-track-archive) (NOAA NCEI): every storm of every agency, every six hours, with the 1-minute wind of the US agencies where there is one. NCEI publishes the last three complete seasons and the storms active now; storms of this season that have already ended arrive with the next complete season.

**Categories** are Saffir-Simpson’s, from the 1-minute wind: tropical depression under 34 kt, tropical storm to 63, then categories 1 (64–82), 2 (83–95), 3 (96–112), 4 (113–136) and 5 (137 and over). JTWC calls a typhoon of 130 kt or more a *super typhoon*.

**Wind and pressure.** NOAA’s [GFS](https://www.emc.ncep.noaa.gov/emc/pages/numerical_forecast_systems/gfs.php) model, 10 m wind, sea-level pressure and rain, from [PacIOOS’s ERDDAP](https://pae-paha.pacioos.hawaii.edu/erddap/griddap/ncep_global.html), which keeps every run since 2022: over the storm’s life (its last nine days at most) every six hours, and the next two days every three, a degree apart, in a box a day that follows the storm 15 degrees of latitude and 20 of longitude around it. A degree (about 110 km) blurs a typhoon’s eye: GFS gives a storm far less wind than the advisories do. The **GFS low** is the lowest pressure within three degrees of where the advisory puts the storm at the same hour, the advisory’s position being interpolated between its fixes. Model and advisory are different forecasts: where they part, the storm’s future is uncertain. Over high ground the isobars crowd for want of a sea: the pressure there is carried down to a sea level kilometres below the ground (the Himalaya, the Andes), so read those bands as mountains.

**Clouds and rain from space.** NASA’s [GIBS](https://nasa-gibs.github.io/gibs-api-docs/) serves the clean infrared (band 13, 10.3 µm) of GOES-West, GOES-East and Himawari every ten minutes; the map takes the satellite nearest overhead the storm (GOES-West west of 106° W, GOES-East to 0°, Himawari east of 70° E) and one picture an hour, the newest of the hour and a half before it. Cold cloud tops, the tall storms, are coloured, from green to red and black. GIBS holds no Meteosat, so a storm off Africa or in the western Indian Ocean has no clouds here. The rain is [IMERG](https://gpm.nasa.gov/data/imerg) early run, every half hour from the GPM constellation and the geostationary infrared, about six hours behind: from there on the blue dots are GFS’s forecast. Your browser asks GIBS for each picture.

**Wind chance** is the National Hurricane Center’s and JTWC’s probability of tropical-storm-force winds (34 kt) at each place within the next five days, from the latest advisory, in bands of ten percent, as [Esri’s Living Atlas](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=248e7b5827a34b248647afb012c58787) republishes it; a storm that has ended has none.

**Freshness.** The gateway keeps each GDACS answer a quarter of an hour and each day of GFS three hours; the satellite and the wind chance are asked for at every load; IBTrACS six hours; the dashboard reloads every 30 minutes. Everything you brush is answered in your browser (Chaski, DuckDB-WASM).

         round((f -> '$.properties.severitydata.severity')::DOUBLE / 1.852)::INTEGER AS peak_kt,
         (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE                    AS latitude,
         (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE                    AS longitude
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
),
-- Active: an advisory in the last day. Advisories come every six hours (three
-- near a coast), so a storm a day without one has ended.
recent AS (
  SELECT *, last_advisory >= now()::TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 1 DAY AS active
  FROM events
  WHERE last_advisory >= now()::TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 14 DAY
)
SELECT CASE WHEN active THEN name ELSE name || ' · ended ' || strftime(last_advisory, '%d %b') END AS __text,
       id AS __value
FROM recent
ORDER BY active DESC, CASE WHEN active THEN -peak_kt END, last_advisory DESC

query.rawSql:
-- The storm picked above, from GDACS's list of tropical cyclones: its last
-- position and the episode (the advisory) GDACS drew last. Through the gateway
-- (feeds), which keeps every GDACS answer a quarter of an hour: GDACS takes
-- 3 to 15 s to build each, and the panels here ask for the same ones nine times.
SET VARIABLE storm = (
  SELECT {id: f ->> '$.properties.eventid',
          episode: f ->> '$.properties.episodeid',
          name: regexp_replace(f ->> '$.properties.eventname', '-[0-9]+$', ''),
          lon: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[0]')::DOUBLE,
          lat: (f -> '$.geometry.coordinates[1]')::DOUBLE}
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?eventlist=TC&alertlevel=green;orange;red',
                       columns = {'features': 'JSON[]'}))
  WHERE f ->> '$.properties.eventid' = $storm);
-- Its advisories are in a "timeline" whose id only the event's own data gives.
SET VARIABLE timeline = (
  SELECT regexp_extract(j ->> '$.properties.impacts[0].resource.timeline', 'id=([0-9]+)', 1)
  FROM read_json_objects('http://feeds/gdacs/events/geteventdata?eventtype=TC&eventid=' || getvariable('storm').id) AS t(j));
-- Server side: the storm picked above, hour by hour, from its first advisory to
-- the end of the GFS forecast on the map (two days ahead), between the
-- advisories (six hours apart) and the forecast (twelve) in straight lines.
-- One row an hour: what the time brush, the 3D curtain, the moving storm and
-- the charts of this tab all read, in the browser.
WITH
-- One row per fix: each advisory's position, then the latest advisory's
-- forecast. GDACS gives the winds in m/s; the advisories give whole knots, so
-- they round back exactly. Longitudes are unwrapped around the storm's last
-- position, so a track across the antimeridian stays one line.
fixes AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT strptime(i ->> 'advisory_datetime', '%d %b %Y %H:%M')                    AS time,
         i ->> 'actual' = 'True'                                                  AS observed,
         (i ->> 'latitude')::DOUBLE                                               AS latitude,
         (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE
           + 360 * round((getvariable('storm').lon - (i ->> 'longitude')::DOUBLE) / 360) AS longitude,
         round((i ->> 'wind_speed')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS wind_kt,
         round((i ->> 'wind_gusts')::DOUBLE / 0.514444)::INTEGER                  AS gust_kt,
         nullif((i ->> 'pressure')::DOUBLE, 0)                                    AS pressure_hpa,
         TRY_CAST(i ->> 'pop39' AS BIGINT)                                        AS people_39mph
  FROM (SELECT unnest(channel.item) AS i
        FROM read_json('http://feeds/gdacs/export/gettimeline?id=' || getvariable('timeline'),
                       columns = {'channel': 'STRUCT(item JSON[])'}))
  -- A time given twice (an observed fix and an old forecast for it) keeps the fix.
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY time ORDER BY observed DESC) = 1
),
span AS (
  SELECT min(time) AS t_first,
         max(time) FILTER (WHERE observed) AS t_last_fix,
         least(max(time), time_bucket(INTERVAL 3 HOUR, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - INTERVAL 90 MINUTE)
                          + INTERVAL 48 HOUR) AS t_last
  FROM fixes
),
hours AS (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(t_first, t_last, INTERVAL 1 HOUR)) AS time FROM span
),
-- Each fix with the next one, and each hour with the fix it follows: at or
-- after that fix, before the next.
segments AS (
  SELECT time AS ta, lead(time) OVER w AS tb,
         latitude AS lat_a, lead(latitude) OVER w AS lat_b,
         longitude AS lon_a, lead(longitude) OVER w AS lon_b,
         wind_kt AS wind_a, lead(wind_kt) OVER w AS wind_b,
         gust_kt AS gust_a, lead(gust_kt) OVER w AS gust_b
  FROM fixes
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY time)
),
between_fixes AS (
  SELECT h.time, s.*
  FROM hours h
  JOIN segments s ON h.time >= s.ta AND (s.tb IS NULL OR h.time < s.tb)
),
hourly AS (
  SELECT time,
         coalesce(epoch(time - ta) / epoch(tb - ta), 0)                      AS k,
         lat_a + coalesce(lat_b - lat_a, 0) * k                               AS latitude,
         lon_a + coalesce(lon_b - lon_a, 0) * k                               AS longitude,
         round(wind_a + coalesce(wind_b - wind_a, 0) * k)                     AS wind_kt,
         round(gust_a + coalesce(gust_b - gust_a, 0) * k)                     AS gust_kt,
         -- The speed the storm moves at: the distance between the two fixes over the time between them.
         ST_Distance_Sphere(ST_Point(lat_a, lon_a), ST_Point(lat_b, lon_b)) / 1000
           / (epoch(tb - ta) / 3600)                                          AS speed_kmh
  FROM between_fixes
),
shaped AS (
  SELECT *,
         CASE WHEN time <= (SELECT t_last_fix FROM span) THEN 'Observed' ELSE 'Forecast' END AS phase,
         -- The change of the wind over the last day: 30 kt or more is rapid intensification.
         wind_kt - lag(wind_kt, 24) OVER (ORDER BY time)                       AS dwind_24h
  FROM hourly
)
SELECT time,
       getvariable('storm').name                                              AS storm,
       round(latitude, 3)                                                     AS latitude,
       round(longitude, 3)                                                    AS longitude,
       wind_kt::INTEGER                                                       AS wind_kt,
       gust_kt::INTEGER                                                       AS gust_kt,
       -- Saffir-Simpson, on the advisory's 1-minute sustained wind in knots.
       CASE WHEN wind_kt >= 137 THEN 'Category 5' WHEN wind_kt >= 113 THEN 'Category 4'
            WHEN wind_kt >= 96 THEN 'Category 3' WHEN wind_kt >= 83 THEN 'Category 2'
            WHEN wind_kt >= 64 THEN 'Category 1' WHEN wind_kt >= 34 THEN 'Tropical storm'
            ELSE 'Tropical depression' END                                 AS category,
       phase,
       -- The same wind twice, one column per phase, so a chart can draw the forecast fainter.
       CASE WHEN phase = 'Observed' THEN wind_kt END                          AS wind_obs,
       CASE WHEN phase = 'Forecast' THEN wind_kt END                          AS wind_fc,
       dwind_24h::INTEGER                                                     AS dwind_24h,
       CASE WHEN dwind_24h >= 30 THEN 'Rapid intensification' WHEN dwind_24h >= 5 THEN 'Intensifying'
            WHEN dwind_24h <= -30 THEN 'Rapid weakening' WHEN dwind_24h <= -5 THEN 'Weakening'
            WHEN dwind_24h IS NOT NULL THEN 'Steady' END                      AS trend,
       round(speed_kmh, 1)                                                    AS speed_kmh,
       -- The present hour, the same on every row: where the charts draw "now".
       date_trunc('hour', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')                          AS now_hour,
       'now'                                                                  AS now_label
FROM shaped
ORDER BY time

-- Server side: every storm of the last three seasons in IBTrACS (NOAA NCEI's
-- best tracks, gathered from every agency), and the storms active now, every
-- six hours: about 7,500 rows for the charts and the map of this tab. Through
-- the gateway (feeds), which keeps both files six hours.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT SID, SEASON, BASIN, NAME, ISO_TIME, LAT, LON, USA_WIND, WMO_WIND, USA_PRES, WMO_PRES, TRACK_TYPE,
         false AS active
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/ibtracs/last3years.csv', all_varchar = true)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT SID, SEASON, BASIN, NAME, ISO_TIME, LAT, LON, USA_WIND, WMO_WIND, USA_PRES, WMO_PRES, TRACK_TYPE,
         true AS active
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/ibtracs/ACTIVE.csv', all_varchar = true)
),
fixes AS (
  SELECT SID AS sid, SEASON::INTEGER AS season, BASIN AS basin, NAME AS name, ISO_TIME::TIMESTAMP AS time,
         LAT::DOUBLE AS latitude, LON::DOUBLE AS longitude,
         -- The US agencies' 1-minute wind where there is one (JTWC, NHC), the WMO agency's otherwise.
         coalesce(TRY_CAST(USA_WIND AS INTEGER), TRY_CAST(WMO_WIND AS INTEGER)) AS wind_kt,
         coalesce(TRY_CAST(USA_PRES AS INTEGER), TRY_CAST(WMO_PRES AS INTEGER)) AS pressure_hpa,
         active
  FROM raw
  -- The second row is units; the main track only (provisional for a storm still
  -- active); the synoptic hours only.
  WHERE SEASON ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND TRACK_TYPE IN ('main', 'PROVISIONAL')
    AND hour(ISO_TIME::TIMESTAMP) % 6 = 0 AND minute(ISO_TIME::TIMESTAMP) = 0
  -- A storm in both files keeps the active copy, which is newer.
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY SID, ISO_TIME ORDER BY active DESC) = 1
),
storms AS (
  SELECT sid, max(wind_kt) AS peak_kt,
         -- Days with winds of tropical-storm strength (34 kt) or more.
         round(count(*) FILTER (WHERE wind_kt >= 34) / 4, 2) AS days,
         bool_or(active) AND max(time) >= now()::TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL 3 DAY AS active_now
  FROM fixes
  GROUP BY sid
)
SELECT f.sid, f.name, f.season,
       CASE f.basin WHEN 'NA' THEN 'North Atlantic' WHEN 'EP' THEN 'East Pacific' WHEN 'WP' THEN 'West Pacific'
                    WHEN 'NI' THEN 'North Indian' WHEN 'SI' THEN 'South Indian' WHEN 'SP' THEN 'South Pacific'
                    ELSE 'South Atlantic' END                                           AS basin,
       f.time, month(f.time)                                                            AS month,
       strftime(f.time, '%b')                                                           AS month_name,
       f.latitude, f.longitude, f.wind_kt, f.pressure_hpa,
       -- Saffir-Simpson, on the advisory's 1-minute sustained wind in knots.
       CASE WHEN f.wind_kt >= 137 THEN 'Category 5' WHEN f.wind_kt >= 113 THEN 'Category 4'
            WHEN f.wind_kt >= 96 THEN 'Category 3' WHEN f.wind_kt >= 83 THEN 'Category 2'
            WHEN f.wind_kt >= 64 THEN 'Category 1' WHEN f.wind_kt >= 34 THEN 'Tropical storm'
            ELSE 'Tropical depression' END                                 AS category,
       s.peak_kt, s.days,
       -- The storms active now again, for a ring around them on the chart of storms.
       CASE WHEN s.active_now THEN s.peak_kt END                                         AS active_peak_kt,
       CASE WHEN s.active_now THEN s.days END                                            AS active_days
FROM fixes f JOIN storms s USING (sid)
WHERE f.wind_kt IS NOT NULL AND s.days > 0
ORDER BY f.sid, f.time
